newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close up on covering, cash action.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close up on covering, cash action.

text.p: Brisk fed cattle sales Tuesday sparked short covering in the CME live cattle pit and boosted futures to higher closes, traders said. Feeder cattle futures also closed up on spillover support and buying linked to strength in cash feeder cattle prices and lower corn futures.

Commercial buying in futures linked to the active fed cattle trade prompted another round of short covering late in live cattle futures. Cash trade was expected to be slow and under pressure going into the holiday. But packers paid prices steady with Monday's tops, which offset some of the lingering bearishness from Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report, they said.

Futures appeared oversold after Monday's selloff which came mostly on fund liquidation in December. Reports that packers were picking up previously purchased fed cattle more quickly than expected added to early strength, they added.
E.D.& F. Man, R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock and RBH bought December while Lind-Waldock and ING bought February. Refco sold both months early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, Cargill Investor Services sold the April 64 straddle. Commercials sold February 62 and 64 puts early and lightly bought October 64 calls. FIMAT spread long February live cattle 64 calls and sold March feeder cattle 62 puts, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures advanced from the start on a sharp rise in the latest CME feeder cattle index. Higher live cattle futures and lower corn futures also provided support but persistent selling by E.D.& F. Man in January put a lid on the market. LIT division of First Options also sold January the latter part of the day, traders said.
The latest index was up $0.99 at $64.25 per cwt, the highest level since December 14, 1995.
ADM Investor Services and locals bought January early and RBH and locals were buyers late, traders said. Rolling of December longs weighed on December at times.
Live cattle closed up 0.275 to 0.425 cent a lb with December up the least at 66.100 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.375 to 0.575 cent higher with January up the least at 65.200 cents.
